title: Compound interest - monthly compounding growth over time
learningObjectives: Explain that compound interest is interest earned on both the initial amount and previously earned interest.
Calculate how a $100 deposit at 5% per year grows to $105 after one year and $110.25 after two years because interest is earned on prior interest.
Describe how saving $730 and investing at 5% grows to $931.69 after five years and $3,155.02 after 30 years.

explanations.text: Compound interest means earnings in one period generate additional earnings later because it is interest earned on interest.

evidence.quote: Compound interest is the interest you earn on interest.

explanations.text: A $100 deposit earning 5% once per year grows to $105 after one year and to $110.25 after two years because the second year includes $0.25 of interest on the first year's $5.

evidence.quote: if you have $100 and it earns 5% interest each year, you'll have $105 at the end of the first year.
At the end of the second year, you'll have $110.25.

explanations.text: The power of compounding over long periods is shown when $730 saved and invested at 5% becomes $931.69 after five years and $3,155.02 after 30 years.

evidence.quote: If you give up pizza and save the $730 for the year, then invest it, earning 5% interest, after five years, you'll have how much? [The correct answer is $931.69.]
How much will you have after 30 years? [The correct answer is $3,155.02.]

predictions.prompt: Predict the amount after 10 years for $100 at 5% compounded monthly.
Predict the amount after 5 years for $730 at 5% compounded yearly.
Predict the amount after 30 years for $730 at 5% compounded yearly.
